sources.entry: SuggestArr | Companion tool for Overseerr and Jellyfin that provides media recommendations.

summary.one_liner: SuggestArr is a self-hosted companion tool that turns users' recent watch history from Jellyfin, Plex or Emby into recommendations and sends the resulting download requests to Seer.
summary.what_it_does: It reads recently watched content from Jellyfin, Plex or Emby, with optional per-user Trakt and Simkl history and imported watch history (CSV or manual TMDb titles with ratings). It finds similar titles through TMDb or through any OpenAI-compatible LLM (such as OpenAI, Ollama, OpenRouter or LiteLLM), with a short reason for each pick. Suggestions are sent to Seer as requests, optionally after manual approval. It can also import public lists from MDBList or Trakt, run AI Search from plain-language descriptions, and clean up old unfavorited requests (dry-run by default). A web interface handles setup, scheduling, users, requests and live logs, and a public REST API with Swagger UI is available at /api/v1.
use_cases: automatically request movies and shows similar to what family members watch
get media recommendations from Jellyfin, Plex or Emby watch history
send recommended titles to Seer for download
import a public MDBList or Trakt list into media requests
search for something to watch using plain-language descriptions
clean up old unwanted media requests
how_to_run: Create a docker-compose.yml with the suggestarr service (image ciuse99/suggestarr:latest) and a ./config_files volume
Open the web interface on the configured port (default 5000)
Follow the setup wizard to connect TMDb, your media server and Seer
notable: Works with Jellyfin, Plex and Emby as watch-history sources and sends requests to Seer
Optional AI recommendations via any OpenAI-compatible LLM, with a reason for each pick
Request control: approval step, pausing while requests are pending, auto-declining stale Seerr requests
Public versioned REST API at /api/v1 with Swagger UI and OpenAPI documents
Cleanup automation that is dry-run by default
caveats: Requires a TMDb API key and a running Jellyfin, Plex or Emby server plus Seer
Optional features such as Trakt, Simkl and LLM recommendations need separate app or API setup
README does not describe platform limits beyond Docker (recommended) or Python 3 installs
